def score_report_line(name, points):
    """Hey! We're putting together the little scoreboard printout for game night,
    and every line has to follow one simple format so the columns stay tidy.
    Return exactly the string '<NAME> scored <points> point(s)' where <NAME> is
    name converted to UPPERCASE and <points> is the int points. Nothing fancy
    here — you're just gluing the pieces together into one line. Use exactly the
    literal text ' scored ' and ' point(s)' with single spaces as shown. That's
    the whole job; even an empty name still gets its line, spacing and all, as
    you can see in the second example below.

    >>> score_report_line('ana', 3)
    'ANA scored 3 point(s)'
    >>> score_report_line('', 0)
    ' scored 0 point(s)'
    """
